# Required object state

The input must be a `GRNData` object with paired RNA and ATAC cells, gene annotation, regulatory regions, and motif matches from `find_motifs()`.

For RegCompass, regulatory regions are normally initialized from the predefined phastCons + SCREEN cCRE union before motif matching. The conditional model uses the paired-cell predictor `RNA(TF) * ATAC(peak)`; RNA and ATAC inputs therefore have to refer to the same cells.

# Production conditional GRN

The production conditional engine is fixed to E-star/JSE with `z = 0.25`. There is no alternative-z grid, conditional ridge-CV lambda, fusion-ratio parameter, or data-driven sensitivity selection in this workflow.

```r
fit_object <- infer_condition_grn(
  grn_object,
  cell_type_col = "cell_type",
  condition_col = "condition",
  genes = metabolic_genes,
  tf_cor = 0.05,
  peak_cor = 0.05,
  min_cells_per_condition = 300L,
  padj_threshold = 0.05,
  rank_action = "mark",
  min_residual_df = 1L,
  parallel = TRUE
)
```

The parameters normally adjusted for a dataset are:

- `tf_cor`, `peak_cor`: absolute Pando candidate-discovery correlation thresholds; both default to `0.05`.
- `min_cells_per_condition`: minimum paired cells retained for each condition.
- `small_condition_action`: `"error"`, `"drop_condition"`, or `"skip_cell_type"` for undersized conditions.
- `padj_threshold`: strict BH threshold for condition-edge support; `padj == padj_threshold` is not significant.
- `rank_action`, `min_residual_df`: estimability and residual-degree-of-freedom controls.
- `parallel`, `BPPARAM`, `parallel_scope`: execution controls.

Conditional ridge/CV controls such as `condition_ridge_control`, `lambda_grid`, `lambda_rule`, and `cv_folds`, as well as `scheme_e_z`, `z`, and `fusion_ratio`, are obsolete on this route and are rejected rather than silently ignored. Standard one-condition `infer_grn()` keeps its independent standard-model controls.

For `K >= 3`, the E-star geometry uses a design ordering of conditions. The current API takes the first retained condition as the predefined reference and records it in `reference_condition`; therefore the input condition ordering must be fixed by the experimental design before fitting and must not be rearranged after inspecting the GRN result. When the reference coordinate is not identifiable for an exact edge, the solver uses an identifiable non-reference contrast first and completes the spanning tree with zero-information boundary coordinates.

# Common exact-edge dictionary

For each broad cell type, Pando runs candidate discovery on all eligible-condition cells pooled together and independently in every condition. Exact `(target, TF, region)` triples passing both configured correlation gates in the pooled/global calculation or in at least one condition are deduplicated into one frozen dictionary.

Every retained condition then uses exactly the same ordered edge dictionary. Candidate correlation support is provenance only after the dictionary is frozen; it is not reapplied as a condition-local topology filter.

Each exact edge uses an equal-condition within-condition RMS scale,

\[
s_e = \sqrt{K^{-1}\sum_c n_c^{-1}\sum_i(x_{cie}-\bar x_{ce})^2},
\]

while the Gaussian information retains the real condition cell counts through `X_c'X_c`. There is no `n_total / (K n_c)` condition-size equalization.

# E-star production coefficient

For stacked condition coefficients, E-star uses

\[
\beta = A\mu + R\delta, \qquad A^T Q R = 0, \qquad D R = I.
\]

The shared component is the unpenalized joint MLE and is not shrunk toward zero. Only identifiable deviation coordinates are penalized:

\[
\hat\delta = \arg\min_\delta\left[\frac12\delta^T H\delta-r^T\delta+0.25\sum_j\sqrt{I_j}|\delta_j|\right].
\]

For a scalar contrast this reduces to

\[
\hat\delta = \operatorname{sign}(d)\left(|d|-0.25/\sqrt{I}\right)_+.
\]

The full spanning contrast tree is retained in the production geometry. If a tree coordinate has zero profile information, its deviation is fixed exactly to zero and is marked `shared_by_boundary`; an identifiable coordinate shrunk exactly to zero is instead marked `fused_by_penalty`. These are different audit states.

`estimate` and `penalty_effect` are the same continuous production E-star coefficient in raw TF-by-ATAC units. Joint inference never overwrites them.

# Fusion-component joint inference

Exact-zero tree deviations define per-edge fusion components. After the E-star structure is frozen, Pando constructs the equality-constrained reduced joint design with condition-specific intercepts and computes the full correlated covariance. This produces inference-only fields:

```text
inference_schema
inference_component_id
inference_hypothesis_id
inference_estimate
inference_se
inference_statistic
inference_estimable
pval
```

Shared or partially shared edge components therefore borrow uncertainty information across the conditions in the same component while retaining covariance with the other correlated TF-by-ATAC predictors.

Raw P values are adjusted separately within each `condition x target` family. The coefficient table records `bh_scope = "condition_target_BH"` and the corresponding family size.

# Exact-edge RegCompass union

For an exact edge `e`, Pando records whether every condition has a valid production coefficient and whether at least one condition has `padj < padj_threshold`. The RegCompass admission rule is:

\[
\text{edge_union_supported}_e =
\left[\forall c:\;\text{fit_status}_{c,g(e)}=\text{"ok"}\;\land\;\beta^E_{c,e}\text{ finite}\right]
\land
\left[\exists c:\;q_{c,e}<\text{padj_threshold}\right].
\]

If an exact edge is admitted, `active_in_regcompass = TRUE` for every condition row of that edge. A nonsignificant small condition therefore keeps its own continuous `penalty_effect`; it is not converted into a missing edge merely because its local power is lower.

`active` / `pando_estimation_active` and `active_in_regcompass` have different meanings: the former indicates a finite production E-star coefficient on the frozen dictionary, whereas the latter indicates admission to the common RegCompass topology.

Target full-data `R2 = 1 - RSS/TSS` is retained as a model diagnostic. It is not a conditional handoff gate and is not used to select `z`.

# Outputs

Use `condition_grn_fit()` to retrieve the complete fit contract. Important coefficient fields include:

```text
target tf region edge_id condition z
estimate penalty_effect beta_shared condition_deviation
contrast_identifiable shared_by_boundary boundary_condition
fused_by_penalty fusion_component_id shared_edge
raw_information_condition profile_information
inference_estimate inference_se inference_statistic inference_estimable
pval padj bh_scope bh_family_size condition_significant
edge_union_supported supporting_conditions n_supporting_conditions
all_conditions_fit_valid active_in_regcompass
rsq fit_status solver_status objective kkt_residual iterations
```

`condition_grn_subgraph(..., significant_only = TRUE)` and `project_condition_grn_cells(..., significant_only = TRUE)` use the exact-edge union handoff, not condition-local significance.

```r
fit <- condition_grn_fit(fit_object, cell_type = "T_cell")

edges <- condition_grn_subgraph(
  fit,
  condition = "Control",
  significant_only = TRUE
)

projection <- project_condition_grn_cells(
  fit_object,
  fit = fit,
  significant_only = TRUE
)

metacell_projection <- aggregate_condition_grn_projection(
  projection,
  membership,
  group_col = "metacell_id"
)
```

Projection uses the admitted condition's continuous `penalty_effect * RNA(TF) * ATAC(peak)` on paired cells and aggregates only after cell-level regulatory scores are computed.
